location.note: Winery point on Highway 29 (987 St. Helena Hwy). The vineyard is next to the winery; its outline is not mapped here yet.

claims.text: Kronos Vineyard lies between Rutherford and St. Helena.
The vines were planted in 1971 on St. George rootstock and are farmed organically.
Cathy Corison bought the property in 1995 after looking for Bale gravelly loam, the alluvial soil of the Rutherford Bench.
Owner recollection: loam, gravel and clay, with an ancient river crossing the property.

soil.status: mapped by the USDA soil survey
soil.note: The USDA soil survey (SSURGO) maps the winery point and everything within 150 m as one map unit, Pleasanton loam, 0 to 2 percent slopes. Layer values are the survey's representative values for that soil, not a sample dug at this vineyard.

reported.note: The 2024 interview says Cathy Corison was looking for Bale gravelly loam when she bought the site. The survey does not map Bale here; only the winery's own soil records could confirm which soil the vines are on.

soil.taxonomic_class: Fine-loamy, mixed, superactive, thermic Mollic Haploxeralfs
soil.overview: The Pleasanton series is a member of the fine-loamy, mixed, thermic family of Mollic Haploxeralfs.  Typically, Pleasanton soils have grayish brown, slightly acid or neutral, gravelly fine sandy loam A horizons; brown, neutral, gravelly sandy clay loam B2t horizons; and gravelly fine sandy loam C horizons.
soil.setting: The Pleasanton soils are on nearly level to gently sloping alluvial fans and terraces at elevations of less than 2,400 feet.  They are in a subhumid, mesothermal climate with hot, dry summers and cool, moist winters.  Mean annual precipitation ranges from 12 to 39 inches.  Average January temperature is 48 degrees F.; average July temperature is about 73 degrees F.; mean annual temperature is about 59 degrees F.; and the freeze-free season is about 220 to 300 days.
soil.range:
Solum thickness to the bottom of the B horizon is 60 inches.  The soils become moist in November or early December and remain moist until May.  Mean annual temperature is about 59 degrees to 64 degrees F.
The A horizon is dark grayish brown, grayish brown, or brown in 10YR or 7.5YR hue.  It is moderately acid to neutral (pH 6.0-7.0).
The B horizon is brown to light yellowish brown in 10YR or 7.5YR hue.  It is loam, sandy clay loam or clay loam and is gravelly or cobbly in some pedons.  It ranges from slightly acid to slightly alkaline.
The C horizon is gravelly fine sandy loam or loam.  It is neutral or mildly alkaline and is slightly calcareous in some pedons.
soil.use: The soils are used for dry farmed grain and grain hay, wine grapes, deciduous fruits, nuts, roses and row crops.  Vegetation is annual grasses and forbs with scattered oaks.
soil.type_location: Alameda County, California; about 5 miles SE of the center of Livermore; SE1/4 NE1/4 NE1/4 sec. 24, T.3S., R.2E. Altamont Quad. lat.37 degrees N. 39 minutes, 45 seconds, long 121 W. 41 minutes, 48 seconds.

horizons.name: Ap
horizons.narrative: Ap--0 to 9 inches; grayish brown (10YR 5/2) gravelly fine sandy loam, very dark grayish brown (10YR 3/2) moist; massive; hard, friable, slightly sticky, slightly plastic; many very fine, common fine and medium roots; common very fine and fine interstitial pores; slightly acid (pH 6.3); abrupt smooth boundary.  (5 to 10 inches thick)

horizons.name: A
horizons.narrative: A1--9 to 21 inches; grayish brown (10YR 5/2) gravelly fine sandy loam, very dark grayish brown (10YR 3/2) moist; massive; hard, friable, slightly sticky, slightly plastic; many very fine, common fine and medium roots; common very fine and fine interstitial pores; neutral (pH 6.8); clear smooth boundary.  (10 to 14 inches thick)

horizons.name: Bt1
horizons.narrative: B2t--21 to 48 inches; brown (10YR 4/3) gravelly sandy clay loam, dark brown (10YR 3/3) moist; moderate medium subangular blocky structure; very hard, friable, sticky, plastic; common very fine and fine roots; many very fine and fine, few medium tubular pores; common moderately thick clay films on peds and in pores; neutral (pH 7.3); gradual wavy boundary.  (12 to 32 inches thick)

horizons.name: Bt2
horizons.narrative: B2t--21 to 48 inches; brown (10YR 4/3) gravelly sandy clay loam, dark brown (10YR 3/3) moist; moderate medium subangular blocky structure; very hard, friable, sticky, plastic; common very fine and fine roots; many very fine and fine, few medium tubular pores; common moderately thick clay films on peds and in pores; neutral (pH 7.3); gradual wavy boundary.  (12 to 32 inches thick)

horizons.name: Bt3
horizons.narrative: B3--48 to 64 inches; brown (10YR 4/3) gravelly loam; dark brown (10YR 3/3) moist; weak medium subangular blocky structure; very hard, friable, sticky, plastic; few very fine roots; many very fine, common fine pores; few thick and few thin clay films on peds and in pores; neutral (pH 7.3); gradual wavy boundary.  (8 to 20 inches thick)
